# buttons.inline

Group supported native inline buttons into rows and produce reply markup.

## Signature

```python
def buttons.inline(rows: collections.abc.Sequence[collections.abc.Sequence[Any]]) -> ReplyInlineMarkup
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Python type | Default | Passing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rows` | `collections.abc.Sequence[collections.abc.Sequence[Any]]` | `Required` | Positional or keyword |

### rows

Nonempty sequence of nonempty keyboard rows. Each row contains supported native inline KeyboardButton variants; reply-only phone/contact request buttons are rejected.

## Returns

types.ReplyInlineMarkup.

## Example

```python
from gramflux import Client, Session, buttons, filters
from gramflux.raw import types

keyboard = buttons.inline([[buttons.callback("Confirm", "yes"), buttons.url("Project", "https://github.com/gramflux/gramflux")]])
await client.send_message("me", "Choose", reply_markup=keyboard)
```

## Constraints and failure behavior

Rows and the outer sequence must be nonempty. Supported kinds are Callback, URL, SwitchInline, InputKeyboardButtonUserProfile, Game and Buy; other keyboard variants fail explicitly.

These examples assume a previously constructed client where one is used. Builders and selectors do not make a network request by themselves. Invalid builder/selector inputs raise ConfigurationError or the underlying Python argument/regex error. Session I/O errors arise when storage is actually opened during connect.
